verified_public_capabilities.finding: Flow can reuse images as ingredients and use start/end frames. These are inputs to generation, not a guarantee of identity or velocity continuity.

The current feature matrix specifies Veo 3.1 Lite for extending eligible 8-second Veo 3.1 clips, including Fast/Quality sources. Quality does not support ingredients; Omni extension is listed as forthcoming.
Flow exposes Extend in the video editor and can save individual video frames. Scenebuilder orders/trims/previews/downloads a sequence. Its documentation excludes other edit modes on extended clips.

The credits table lists Extend alongside Lite/Fast/Quality prices, while the feature matrix limits current extension generation to Lite. Live controls must resolve this discrepancy; do not promise Quality extensions from the price table alone.

findings: Flow's official commercial-use FAQ points to Google's Terms of Service and says Google does not claim ownership of generated original content. This is not a warranty of copyrightability, exclusivity or third-party rights clearance.

Reviewed general Google terms were effective July 30, 2026 in the served US version; Google One terms were last modified November 11, 2025. Applicable account-country terms and any additional live notices must be checked before use if they differ.

Google's published terms require lawful inputs and respect for intellectual property. The Labs service listing links the general terms and Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy. No separate paid commercial-output licence or mandatory textual attribution was identified in these reviewed sources.
Flow documents embedded SynthID and possible visible watermarking, including region-specific requirements. Preserve provider markings; do not add watermark removal to this workflow.
No new terms were accepted in this turn. The review does not approve supplied artwork/music or publishing. YouTube monetization remains a separate channel/content decision.
commercial_review.youtube_implication: Recurring TABI characters can support distinct stories, but changing only a background/outfit does not by itself establish original substantive variation. Avoid treating a reusable production template as automatic Partner Program eligibility.

proposed_defaults.aspect_ratio: 16:9, provided the selected source supports the intended framing
proposed_defaults.camera: Locked to the selected source for this continuous train test
proposed_defaults.source_clip: Choose the strongest existing TABI clip after visual inspection; preserve an untouched local original and its hash
proposed_defaults.reference: A clean frame from that source plus matching existing TABI references; never the rejected native Blender draft
proposed_defaults.generation_model: Use the live supported Extend model; current documented candidate is Veo 3.1 Lite
proposed_defaults.music: No generated score or dialogue requested; keep original local music for finishing later
proposed_defaults.scenery: Inherit exact camera, travel direction and apparent speed from the selected source; landmarks keep moving through the join
proposed_defaults.timing: Measure actual added duration. The documented 8-second generation setting is not proof of eight net new seconds per extension.
proposed_defaults.output: Exactly 90 seconds only after reviewed assembly; source fps must be probed, never assumed

initial_test: Record the source clip's look, pose, cup state, scene layout, exterior movement, model, length, prompt, references and visible credit price. Preserve the source.
Generate one continuation containing only quiet breathing. Inspect the boundary and the full result before using it as the next input.
Continue with a gentle turn toward the existing window. Check that face/gills/headphones stay stable and the scenery carries forward without reset.
Continue the accepted branch with a relaxed window-looking hold. Compare beginning, middle and end to the original, including ears, collar, hands, cup and environment landmarks.
Allow at most one repair from the last clean ancestor. A drifting final frame must not become a new canonical character reference.
If this roughly 30-second sequence passes, scale cautiously toward the complete 90-second story. Do not replace the requested continuous shot with a montage or conceal drift with dissolves.
prompt_use: Prepared instructions, not submitted prompts. Inspect the clip first, then adapt window direction, source pose and prop state without contradicting visible evidence. Apply the continuity prefix plus only the current beat, not the entire 90-second action list. Exact timings in the story are editorial targets rather than guaranteed model outputs.
continuity_prefix: Continue the existing shot from its current final moment. Preserve the exact same TABI character design, facial proportions, gills, headphones, outfit, body shape and tail. Keep one continuous camera view, the same train interior, seat, table, cup, lighting and framing. Continue the scenery already passing outside at the same speed and in the same direction, with natural ongoing parallax and no restart or reversal. Keep the character's anatomy coherent, with one pair of arms and hands and the head naturally connected to the body. Maintain gentle visible breathing. No shot change, redesign, new objects, dialogue, captions or music.

initial_beat_prompts.name: quiet_continuation
initial_beat_prompts.prompt: TABI stays in the current seated pose and breathes slowly, with a small natural rise and fall of the chest and shoulders and one relaxed blink. The hands remain in their current resting position. The cup stays exactly where it is. Keep the movement calm throughout.

initial_beat_prompts.name: look_outside
initial_beat_prompts.prompt: From the current pose, TABI slowly turns his eyes and then his head a little toward the existing train window, without moving his seated body or hands. He settles into watching the passing scenery. The turn is small enough to preserve the original head and gill silhouette. Continue gentle breathing.

initial_beat_prompts.name: window_hold
initial_beat_prompts.prompt: TABI continues looking out of the window in the pose reached by the previous shot. He quietly watches the scenery, breathing visibly and blinking once. No extra gesture or camera movement. Keep the passing scenery in uninterrupted motion.

later_action_prompts.name: sip
later_action_prompts.precondition: The same cup is resting within reach in the selected source; hand choice and handle orientation must follow the actual image. Allow multiple sequential continuations if needed for a complete action.
later_action_prompts.prompt: TABI gently reaches for the existing cup, takes a secure natural grip, lifts it to his mouth, takes one small sip, lowers it and returns it to the exact same place on the table. The cup keeps the same shape and orientation; the hand follows it continuously. His other arm stays in its current resting position. Finish with both hands resting and the cup on the table.

later_action_prompts.name: small_sway
later_action_prompts.prompt: With the cup resting on the table and both hands at rest, TABI enjoys an imagined relaxed beat: a tiny rhythmic head and shoulder sway while breathing naturally. Keep the movement restrained and his seated body stable. No generated soundtrack. Finish relaxed.

later_action_prompts.name: deep_breath
later_action_prompts.prompt: TABI takes one clearly visible slow deep breath: chest and shoulders gradually rise, pause comfortably, then settle on a long relaxed exhale. His expression becomes peaceful. Keep the neck connected, gills attached, hands resting and body seated. After the exhale, hold a quiet natural breathing pose as the scenery continues to pass.

story_beats.action: Quiet seated breathing; establish the existing source pose
One complete sip with cup returned to its original position
Visible deep breath and calm finish

acceptance.character: Compare original, intermediate and final frames: same face, gills, headphones, outfit, tail and body proportions; inspect temporal motion for crawling edges, morphing or flicker.
acceptance.anatomy: No disconnected neck, duplicated arms, disappearing hands/gills or broken contact. Body remains seated and coherent through all actions.
acceptance.props: One unchanged cup, continuous reach/grip/sip/return, plausible hand and mouth contact and stable table location.
acceptance.world: No camera/interior/light reset. Track exterior landmarks across joins and verify travel direction, parallax and speed; matching endpoint pixels alone do not pass this gate.
acceptance.story: Complete actions separated by quiet breathing holds; state from the previous segment persists. Exact duration is measured after assembly, with no arbitrary action truncation.
acceptance.workload: Count every attempt, accepted duration, actual credits, elapsed time and user intervention. No monthly-capacity conclusion from advertised generation prices alone.
acceptance.larger_workflow: After a successful train sequence, test a different interior/exterior, a genuinely different outfit, cafe activity and walking. A single train success does not qualify these.

fallbacks_and_limits: If Extend is unavailable, a saved last frame can be a new start frame. This matches composition more closely than a fresh prompt but does not preserve the source video's motion history; run a separate join test.
If the original clip uses a model without Extend, do not silently regenerate it in another model and claim the quality is preserved.
No continuous-length limit or net extension duration has been verified in this account. Do not infer 90-second support from short-clip controls or apply Veo API limits to the Flow web app.
A planned-cut story could tolerate longer-form continuity limits, but it is a different deliverable from the requested uninterrupted train view and requires user agreement.
Flow generates complete-scene pixels, including scenery. Swapping the outside independently after generation is not established by this route.

The proposed video-story role is references, story/continuation state, imported footage, local music and measured export. Built-in Flow generation/API access and subscription coverage are unverified; the current app does not implement that workflow.

credit_planning.reviewed_rates: Published standard Ultra rates: Lite 5, Fast 10, Quality 100 per generation. Lite Lower Priority lists zero for eligible Ultra subscribers/plan managers. Live prices and eligibility take precedence.
credit_planning.monthly_entitlement: Published Ultra tiers list 10000 or 25000 monthly Flow credits plus daily credits. Exact current Flow balance/tier not inspected; previous Colab allowance verification is a different resource.
credit_planning.initial_cap: Up to three extensions plus one repair, one output each, capped at 20 existing credits total. No credit top-up or subscription change.
credit_planning.illustration_not_benchmark: If an episode required 12 accepted units and three attempts per accepted unit, 36 Lite generations at 5 credits would be 180 per episode or 5400 for 30. This assumes the model, net duration and acceptance rate work; it excludes source creation, new assets, other account usage and finishing. It is not a promise of sufficient allowance.
